title: "Individual assignment 2"

## Practice building and publishing a Docker image

The purpose of this assignment is to make sure everyone gets hands-on practice
building a Docker image from a `Dockerfile`
and publishing it to Docker Hub with GitHub Actions.
You will do the same for your team's project in Milestone 2,
there for both Intel/AMD and ARM computers.

### Exercise instructions

1.  Create a **public** repository on GitHub.com under your personal username called `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
    Select the option to create the repository with a `README` file.

2.  In it, make a small project with **either** uv (Python) **or** renv (R)
    that has at least **two** packages,
    each pinned to an exact version.

    -   **uv:** list the packages in `pyproject.toml` with `==`
        (see [uv: pinning exact versions](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-python-uv-exact-pins.html)),
        and commit `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version`.
    -   **renv:** list the packages in `DESCRIPTION` with `(== x.y.z)`, using explicit snapshots
        (see [renv: declaring packages in `DESCRIPTION`](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-r-renv-description.html)),
        and commit `DESCRIPTION`, `renv.lock`, `.Rprofile` and `renv/`
        (the `.gitignore` inside `renv/` keeps the installed packages out).

3.  Add a `Dockerfile` that installs those packages from your lock file:

    -   **uv:** follow [Python packages with uv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-uv.html).
    -   **renv:** follow [R packages with renv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-renv.html).

    Use a base image with a version tag (for example `rocker/r-ver:4.6.2`), not `latest`.

4.  Build the image on your computer and test it:
    run a container from it and load each of your packages.

5.  Publish the image to Docker Hub with GitHub Actions.
    [Building images for several platforms](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-platforms.html)
    walks through these steps; for this assignment, use its single-platform workflow.

    -   Create a free [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/) account if you don't have one,
        and a public Docker Hub repository named `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
    -   Create a Docker Hub [access token](https://docs.docker.com/security/access-tokens/)
        with Read & Write permissions.
    -   In your GitHub repository, add two
        [repository secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)
        (Settings \> Secrets and variables \> Actions \> New repository secret):
        `DOCKER_USERNAME`, your Docker Hub username,
        and `DOCKER_PASSWORD`, the access token (not your Docker Hub password).
    -   Copy the chapter's single-platform workflow into `.github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml`.
        Change only its `IMAGE` line, to `<your-docker-hub-username>/dsci522-dockerfile-practice`, all in lowercase.
        The workflow builds the image and pushes it to Docker Hub,
        tagged `latest` and with the commit SHA,
        whenever a push changes the `Dockerfile` or a lock file,
        or when you run it by hand.
    -   Push, and check that the run on your repository's **Actions** tab succeeds.
        To run it by hand, open the workflow on the **Actions** tab and click **Run workflow**.
    -   If Git refuses to push the workflow file,
        your personal access token needs the **workflow** scope:
        on GitHub, go to Settings \> Developer settings \> Personal access tokens,
        select your token, and tick **workflow**.

6.  Add a `LICENSE.md` that attributes the workflow you copied.
    The workflow comes from [docker-uv-renv](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv),
    so copy the text of its [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv/blob/main/LICENSE) (MIT) into your `LICENSE.md`,
    and add a note that it covers only the code you copied (`.github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml`).

### Submission instructions

Follow the instructions for submission on Gradescope.
We only need URLs, entered into Gradescope directly: there is no PDF to make.
You will submit:

1.  A link to the GitHub.com repository that you create for this assignment.
    -   You should name your GitHub.com repository `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
2.  A link to your Docker image on Docker Hub.
    You should name your Docker Hub repository `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.

## Rubric

This assignment will be graded for completion as follows:

| Grade | Description                                                                                                                            |
|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| -15%  | There were issues with the links submitted that made it difficult to find the GitHub or Docker Hub repository                          |
| -15%  | A package in `pyproject.toml` or `DESCRIPTION` is not pinned to an exact version                                                       |
| -15%  | There were authentication issues with publishing to Docker Hub                                                                         |
| -33%  | Fewer than two packages are listed in `pyproject.toml` or `DESCRIPTION`                                                                |
| -33%  | The Docker image was not built successfully by GitHub Actions and published to Docker Hub                                              |
| -100% | Assignment was not completed (no GitHub repository was created, or the repository is missing the environment files or the `Dockerfile`) |
